counterfactual_missing_items: comprehensive workup—including a TORCH panel, platelet count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, plasminogen levels, von Willebrand factor, factor V Leiden, protein S, protein C, and antiplatelet antibodies—returned within normal limits
Fetal Doppler ultrasound demonstrated normal middle cerebral artery perfusion
decisive_items: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
response.rationale: R5 directly matches the core imaging findings (ventriculomegaly) without any raw contradiction. Other candidates rely on non-specific changes (hyperechoic regions, roughened choroid plexus, MRI signal) that are explicitly disconfirmed by normal infectious and vascular workups, or are implausible given the lack of supporting systemic findings.

rejected.why: Proposed congenital CNS infection is contradicted by the raw span indicating normal TORCH panel and other lab results.
Fetal stroke is explicitly contradicted by normal middle cerebral artery perfusion on Doppler, and its supportive imaging findings overlap with non-stroke conditions.
Neonatal hemochromatosis is unsupported; the MRI signal pattern is non-specific and there is no hepatic or systemic evidence to support this diagnosis.
